findings.claim: Take a Clips Library whose Target is a member Smart Folder that evaluates to tooLarge or failed. On the commit where that Target first becomes ready as `default`, `switchTo` is still set and the URL is unchanged, so `switchPending` is true. `effectiveParams` therefore strips `group`/`sort`, and `Library` mounts with the `default` Target's stored view and sends a grouped-shelves request with it. The effect then clears `switchTo` without a rewrite. The next render reads the old URL's `group`/`sort`, aborts that request and sends another with the previous Target's values. The first request carries a grouping or sort that is not the one finally shown.
findings.impact: An extra Library request goes out with a grouping or sort that is never the one shown, and a loading or wrong-view frame can flash. This is an I8 violation in normal use: picking a member Target that turns out to be too large while on the Library.
findings.evidence: useNotesTarget.ts:127,138,162-166: when the member is unusable, the target is `{status:'ready', key:'default'}` and `selectedId` is 'default'. clips.tsx:154: `switchPending` is true while `switchTo.search === search`. clips.tsx:155-163: `group`/`sort` are stripped, so `view` is the `default` Target's resolved view. clips.tsx:254-255,289-303: `bodyDrawn` is true and `Library` renders, because a new `useScopedLoad` scope gives null data (useScopedLoad.ts:33-37), so `targetHasNone` is false. useGroupedShelves.ts:44-66: the request is sent in an effect keyed on the scope, which includes `by` and `sort`. clips.tsx:211-216: `switchSettled` is true because `targetId` ('default') !== `switchTo.id`. The effect only calls `setSwitchTo(null)`, so the next render reads the old URL's `group`/`sort` (clips.tsx:154-163) and the scope changes again.
findings.repro: Traced in code, not run. On drive D, on Target P (not `default`), choose group=folder. The URL is ?view=all&group=folder&sort=added_desc. The `default` Target's stored group is tag. Choose a member Smart Folder M that evaluates to tooLarge. While M is evaluated the body is a skeleton. When the evaluation answers, the first committed render mounts GroupShelves with by=tag and sends that request. The next render switches to by=folder from the URL, aborts the first request and sends a second. This happens only when P is not `default` and the URL's view differs from the `default` Target's stored view.

bucket_proposal.reason: Normal single-user flow; no crafted input needed. I8 forbids any Library body request with a grouping or sort other than the one finally shown after a Target change.

findings.proposed_fix: When the switch settles because a different Target came into force, decide which values apply in the same render that first shows that Target, before Library mounts. One way is to compute `switchSettled` for the fallback case during render and stop stripping the URL then. Another is to rewrite the URL to the `default` Target's view, if I13 is revised.

verification.note: Reproduced by trace. Next 16.2.1 `router.replace` runs `dispatchNavigateAction` inside `startTransition` (frontend/node_modules/next/dist/client/components/app-router-instance.js:339-341), so the search-param change is a transition. `setSwitchTo(null)` at clips.tsx:220 is an ordinary update and commits first. On that commit `switchPending` is false (clips.tsx:154) and `effectiveParams` keeps the old URL's `group`/`sort` (155-162). `view` is therefore the previous Target's view. `Library` -> `GroupShelves` -> `useGroupShelves` (useGroupedShelves.ts:36,44-66) has a scope that includes `by`/`sort`, so a request goes out with the new Target and the old view. When the transition commits, the scope changes again and a third request goes out. `fillHref` (clips.tsx:256-259) stays null because the old URL is readable. Notes shows the same pattern. The onChoose handler sets `setSwitchingFor(id)` (NotesPage.tsx:165-170), and the effect calls `setSwitchingFor(null)` before `router.replace(...)` (NotesPage.tsx:60-64). After that `ignoreUrlSort` is false (NotesPage.tsx:128), NotesLibrary.tsx:76-78 takes the URL's old `sort`, and `useNotesList` (useNotesList.ts:62, keyed on `sort`) requests with it. The test harness hides this: notesAppHarness.tsx:44-53,64-66,79 applies replace synchronously through `useSyncExternalStore`, so the URL change and the flag change land in one render. This only shows when the previous Target's URL view differs from the new Target's view.

The code does what the finding states. useNotesTarget.ts:127,138,162-166 put `default` in force (target key 'default', selectedId 'default') when the member evaluates to tooLarge/failed. clips.tsx:211-212 then makes `switchSettled` true because 'default' !== `switchTo.id`. The effect at 213-217 only clears `switchTo` and never rewrites, so the URL keeps the previous Target's `group`/`sort`, and readClipsView shows them (clips.tsx:163; I3 gives the URL precedence). Whether this is a defect depends on the spec. I13's last clause says 'a fallback to `default` ... leave[s] the URL's `group` and `sort` as they were', which appears to require this behaviour. That conflicts with I4 (no view parameter left over from the previous Target) and I6 (the view read is the `default` Target's). A human should resolve which invariant governs. A separate transient request in this path is filed as verifier finding V1.

specification_compliance: I8: violated transiently after a Target change in Clips and Notes, because the real router commits replace as a transition after the flag clear (R1). Also violated in the Clips fallback-to-default path (V1).
I4/I6 vs I13: in the Clips fallback to `default` (R2), the URL keeps the previous Target's `group`/`sort`. I13 appears to require this; I4 and I6 appear to forbid it.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The spec does not say which view is shown when a chosen Clips Target falls back to `default` while the URL still holds the previous Target's `group`/`sort`. I13 says to leave the URL as it is, which by I3 shows the previous Target's view; I4 and I6 imply the `default` Target's view.
regression_risks: Any fix that clears the switch flag only after the URL changes must still clear it when the replace targets an identical URL; the Next router treats a same-URL replace as a no-op for search params.
test_coverage: notesAppHarness.tsx applies router.replace synchronously through useSyncExternalStore. The search-param change and the state updates in the same effect land in one render, so no unit test can observe the intermediate render described in R1.
No test was found covering a Clips Target switch to a member Target that becomes tooLarge/failed while on the Library (R2/V1). Not exhaustively searched.
not_verified: The real Next.js commit ordering (transition vs. default-lane update) was traced in source, not observed in a browser.
Did not check whether an e2e suite exercises Target switching on the Clips or Notes Library with the real router.
Did not diff against origin/develop, so whether R1/R2/V1 were introduced by this branch is unverified.
Did not review the Video and Reading apps for the same pattern.
